proposal.title: Droynruk: a small full-text search engine for static sites
proposal.summary: Droynruk builds a small full-text search engine for static sites for authors of documentation sites.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Static sites rely on external search services that track visitors. Authors of documentation sites depend on search every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a small full-text search engine for static sites called Droynruk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Search is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/droynruk/droynruk, which 143 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on search for 11 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/droynruk/droynruk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 73650.00 EUR for 125 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Static sites rely on external search services that track visitors. Authors of documentation sites depend on search every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a small full-text search engine for static sites called Droynruk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Search is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/droynruk/droynruk, which 143 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on search for 11 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/droynruk/droynruk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 73650.00 EUR for 125 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
